set.tovw: Lead grade D (treasure thread): recovery c.1910-12 rumoured, never substantiated; site only to the shore

m-tr-rc-2.st: Clint Dunathan (Escanaba Daily Press, 1946) put the Hole in the Ground 'on the shore about two miles south of Fayette', burned by a mob of about 50 c.1876. In 1946 the site was 'a quiet opening on the sandy shore, growing up in sparse grass', with melted glass and lead-foil bottle covers still visible and 'two large holes dug in the ground where the Hole in the Ground once stood'. The Detroit News (1930) said 'all the caverns in the region were explored' and that the rumour the treasure was found about 20 years earlier 'was never substantiated'.
m-tr-rc-2.t: The melted-glass scatter marks the saloon site. 2015 Michigan 1 m lidar shows no clear pair of large pits on this shore; the only paired dips (about 0.7 m, near 45.6977,-86.6686, about 50 m from the water) lie along an old track and are not convincing. State-forest shore: check access.
src: Escanaba Daily Press, 5 Sep 1946, p. 4, Clint Dunathan column (Newspapers.com 51022761)
